analysis.title: PrimeView: Hedge Funds Add to AI Hedging Shorts
key_insights: On Friday hedge funds kept reducing AI beta, led by Semis (-0.8std), Memory (-1.0std) and Hardware (-1.2std). Flows shifted from over 90% long selling to roughly 50/50 long selling and shorting.
Hyperscalers were small net bought (+0.3std). Hedge funds favored higher-quality names with available compute and stronger build profiles, extending a trend seen since early October.
Power names were net bought (+1.7std), with about 70% of flows from long buying. Hedge funds bottom-fished selectively and added relative-value trades across the AI value chain.

Hedge funds added +1.9std of gross exposure to US equities, the 6th-largest re-risking day YTD. The add came from +2std of short exposure and +1std of long exposure, so it was largely market-neutral/RV rather than a directional bet.
Friday saw the largest increase in hedge fund short exposure since June 15, before the summer unwind.

UBS Head of Cash Equity Trading Zain Nizami remains cautious as correlations rise. The risk is that crowded sector and RV trades, particularly Semis vs. Software and Semis vs. Hyperscalers, spill over into broader portfolio de-risking.
Nizami recommends buying Semis while selling the recent 'hedging beneficiaries'. Net exposure in Semis is back near July and Liberation Day lows, while Hyperscaler and Software exposures remain high.
